Article Title: SJM urges Centre to block Starlink’s rollout
Article Text:
Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM) urged the Centre to block Starlink’s commercial rollout

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: RSS-affiliated Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM) on Tuesday urged the Centre to block Starlink’s commercial rollout, questioning whether Elon Musk ’s satellite broadband service could ensure that Indian traffic passes through domestic gateways and comply with orders to restrict connectivity in specified areas.SJM national co-convener Ashwani Mahajan said the concerns involved India’s capacity to monitor communications lawfully and enforce security restrictions. It argued that laser links between satellites could allow traffic to bypass Indian ground infrastructure and travel through foreign networks.“A key regulatory condition is that Starlink must be able to precisely restrict its services at the govt’s behest,” SJM said. It questioned whether the company could meet this requirement, citing terrorism, riots and protests as situations in which authorities may seek local shutdowns.At issue, in SJM’s argument, is whether Indian authorities can enforce security directives on a foreign operator whose network extends beyond the country’s physical borders. SJM contrasted this with incumbent telecom companies which, it said, cooperate with investigators and can suspend services in designated areas.The group accused Musk of applying public pressure instead of addressing Indian security concerns. Its intervention follows his allegation that “certain oligarchs” were blocking Starlink to protect their businesses and his criticism of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani.SJM also flagged potential misuse by insurgents and smugglers. Starlink equipment was recovered during a drug seizure in Andaman and Nicobar Islands and an army search operation in Manipur in 2024. Musk has maintained that Starlink’s satellite beams were never activated over India.Starlink received a telecom licence on June 6, 2025, and authorisation from space regulator IN-SPACe on July 8 that year. Its commercial launch awaits completion of security assessments and spectrum assignment.On Oct 8, the communications ministry rejected the discrimination allegations as “baseless and misconceived”, saying Starlink, Jio’s satellite venture and Bharti-backed OneWeb were at broadly the same regulatory stage. Each must demonstrate security compliance before seeking spectrum, it said.Starlink has previously said Indian user data would remain within the country and its security controls would meet Indian requirements.Arguing for indigenous alternatives, SJM claimed blocking Starlink would accelerate domestic satellite broadband development and eventually deliver cheaper connectivity to remote areas. It said India’s growing space capabilities and private sector participation could support domestic alternatives, even if their rollout took some more time. It also invoked US trade restrictions, arguing India was entitled to withhold permission on national security grounds.
Article Summary: SJM national co-convener Ashwani Mahajan said the concerns involved India’s capacity to monitor communications lawfully and enforce security restrictions. It argued that laser links between satellites could allow traffic to bypass Indian ground infrastructure and travel through foreign networks.

Article Title: ‘Constitution, not convenience’: Harvard-affiliated Indians hit out at anti-EC protests
Article Text:
Harvard-affiliated Indians flag attacks on constitutional institutions and alleged misuse of the university’s name

‘Evidence, not accusations’

A group of Indian citizens affiliated with Harvard University has raised concerns over what it described as a “concerted campaign” against the country's constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission, the Supreme Court, the office of the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and Parliament.In a statement issued on Wednesday, the signatories also flagged reports of Harvard University's name being used to lend credibility to a political campaign without appropriate authorisation, while calling for greater respect for constitutional values and democratic institutions."We are deeply concerned by the negative public discourse and concerted campaign against India’s constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission of India , the Supreme Court, the office of the Hon’ble Chief Justice of India, and Parliament," the statement said.The signatories expressed concern over public discourse surrounding constitutional authorities, particularly the use of terms such as “thieves” and “compromised” to describe them, and references to India being under “siege”.Such language, they said, raised serious concerns about attempts to undermine public trust in democratic institutions.“The language used to describe India as being under ‘siege’ and to characterise constitutional authorities as ‘thieves’ or ‘compromised’ raises serious concerns about the intent to undermine public trust in democratic institutions,” the statement read.The statement also addressed the role of law enforcement agencies in maintaining public order, saying their actions should be subject to fair scrutiny but that allegations must be grounded in evidence and due process.“The actions of law enforcement agencies to uphold public order deserve fair scrutiny, but sweeping accusations and abusive rhetoric cannot substitute for evidence, due process or institutional accountability,” the signatories said.They also stressed the need to respect public officials and the offices they hold, adding that constitutional principles and civil liberties must not be applied selectively.“The Constitution, rule of law, and civil liberties must be respected at all times, not just when it suits our interests,” the statement said.Summing up their appeal, the signatories said: “Our commitment must remain to the Constitution, not convenience; to justice, not selective outrage; and to democratic institutions, not the politics of accusation.”The signatories listed affiliations with several Harvard schools, including Harvard Medical School, Harvard Kennedy School, Harvard Law School, Harvard Business School, Harvard Extension School, Harvard Divinity School, Harvard TH Chan School of Public Health and Harvard Graduate School of Education.Among those named were AK Raghawan and Abhigyan Satyam of Harvard Medical School; Abhishek M, Banu Nagarajan, Bhavya Bishnoi, Deepanshu Aggarwal, Divya Dwivedi and Jaya Awasthi of Harvard Kennedy School; and Adhitya Srinivasan and Almas Lokhandwala of Harvard Law School.The statement comes as opposition parties and the Cockroach Janta Party have been protesting against the alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls.
Article Summary: Harvard-affiliated Indians flag attacks on constitutional institutions and alleged misuse of the university’s name. They call for greater respect for constitutional values and democratic institutions. The statement comes as opposition parties and the Cockroach Janta Party have been protesting against the alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls.

Article Title: Bomb threat in Air India Frankfurt-Delhi flight: Pilot pressed hijack code; plane diverted to Jaipur
Article Text:
Air India flight (Representative image)

Pilot reportedly used hijack alert code

NEW DELHI: An Air India flight from Frankfurt to Delhi was diverted to Jaipur on Wednesday following a security alert triggered by a suspected hijack threat.The flight, AI-2030, landed safely and was immediately escorted to a designated isolation bay, adhering strictly to standard operating procedures for aviation security emergencies.Assistant Commissioner of Police (Malviya Nagar) Shiv Dayal said airport authorities had alerted the police about the emergency landing following the threat, news agency PTI reported.Police and security personnel were checking the aircraft in the isolation bay, he added.According to preliminary information, the pilot activated Squawk Code 7500, the internationally recognised transponder code indicating hijacking or unlawful interference, while the aircraft was in the Mumbai Flight Information Region (FIR).The aircraft was subsequently diverted to Jaipur, the source said. The number of passengers on board was not immediately known.Following the aircraft's safe landing, the pilots and passengers were deboarded in a phased manner under security supervision, according to the information available. Passengers and their baggage were undergoing security screening.Ground teams from the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), airport security agencies and local police cordoned off the isolation bay and began checking the aircraft.The National Security Guard (NSG) was also placed on standby in New Delhi, according to the information provided. Further details about the security alert and the ongoing investigation were awaited.In a similar incident in August, an Air India Express flight from Dammam, Saudi Arabia, to Delhi made an emergency landing at Ahmedabad airport after a tissue paper bearing the word “bomb” was found in the aircraft’s lavatory.All 32 passengers on board were safely deboarded at Terminal 2, according to Ahmedabad Police.
Article Summary: Air India flight from Frankfurt to Delhi diverted to Jaipur. Pilot reportedly used hijack alert code Squawk Code 7500. The number of passengers on board was not immediately known. In August, an Air India Express flight from Dammam, Saudi Arabia, to Delhi made an emergency landing at Ahmedabad airport after a tissue paper bearing the word “bomb” was found.

Former UK prime minister Rishi Sunak met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Tuesday and congratulated him on completing 25 years in public service. Praising PM Modi’s commitment and work ethic, Sunak said the UK-India relationship was going from “strength to strength” under his leadership.In a post on X, Sunak recalled working with PM Modi during his tenure as prime minister and highlighted the importance of closer cooperation between the two countries in trade, technology and artificial intelligence (AI).“Prime Minister Narendra Modi great to see you in New Delhi today. Congratulations on 25 years in public service, a remarkable achievement. It was a pleasure to work with you when I was Prime Minister,” Sunak wrote.Praising Modi’s approach to public service, he added, “Your commitment, your work ethic, your energy is an example to us all.”On bilateral ties, Sunak said, “The UK India relationship is going from strength to strength under your leadership. Our two countries cooperating more on trade, tech and AI is vital in a less predictable world.”He also expressed confidence in the future of the partnership, writing, “I know that Britain and India will continue to grow ever closer in the years ahead.”Earlier on Tuesday, Sunak spoke about the changing global order and the growing ability of countries such as India and those in the Gulf to pursue independent foreign policy positions amid increasing geopolitical uncertainty.Speaking at a panel discussion titled “The End of Predictability” at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026 in New Delhi, Sunak said the world was moving away from the multilateral, rules-based framework that had shaped the global economy.“We all grew up investing in, operating in a multilateral rules-based framework, largely enforced by US President Trump is not a cause for that; he's a symptom of that, and the world that we're in now is one where we don't quite know what we've settled down to, and that creates an enormous amount of geopolitical uncertainty and indeed danger,” he said.Sunak also described China’s emergence as a strategic competitor to the United States as a significant shift.“So, China is a peer competitor for the US across economic, military, and technological domains. That is a new feature of the world economy,” he said.Meanwhile, India and the UK have agreed to exchange annual data on the utilisation of tariff concessions under their Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA). The decision was taken at the 16th meeting of the India-UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO) in New Delhi on Monday.Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal and UK business secretary Jonathan Reynolds reviewed progress since the agreement came into force on July 15, 2026. The annual data exchange is intended to support smoother implementation and help more businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, benefit from the pact.
Article Summary: Former UK prime minister Rishi Sunak met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Tuesday. Praising PM Modi’s commitment and work ethic, Sunak said the UK-India relationship was going from “strength to strength” under his leadership.

Article Title: 'Agreed to build on positive momentum in ties': PM Modi speaks with Canada PM Mark Carney
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said he had spoken with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, with the two leaders agreeing to build on the positive momentum in India-Canada ties and work towards concrete outcomes across key areas of their strategic partnership.In a post on X, PM Modi described the conversation as “warm and productive” and said the two sides would focus on trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people ties.“Together, India and Canada are contributing towards a more stable and prosperous world,” PM Modi wrote.The conversation comes amid efforts by the two countries to strengthen ties and advance negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), which both sides hope to conclude by December.India and Canada are currently in the fifth round of negotiations for the proposed trade agreement. The two leaders have called for an ambitious and mutually beneficial CEPA that could help increase bilateral trade to 70 billion Canadian dollars (around $49 billion) by 2030.Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney had last month said negotiations were making good progress and expressed his willingness to host PM Modi in Canada in December.The proposed visit is tentatively scheduled for December 11-13, according to official sources.The two sides are hoping to conclude trade negotiations by the end of the year.PM Modi's proposed visit would be his first bilateral trip to Canada since relations were strained by a diplomatic row over the killing of a Khalistan separatist. He last visited Canada in June 2025 to attend the G7 Summit at Carney's invitation.Alongside trade, New Delhi and Ottawa have been seeking to deepen cooperation on security and defence.During the latest round of bilateral security dialogue, both sides welcomed efforts to advance CEPA negotiations and underlined the potential for a more substantive defence relationship.National security adviser Ajit Doval and his Canadian counterpart, David Morrison, also reviewed progress in security and law enforcement cooperation under a shared Security Work Plan concluded in February.In a joint statement, the two sides said they would explore further practical cooperation, including structured dialogues on cyber security and economic security.They also agreed to strengthen coordination against transnational organised crime, terrorism, violent extremism, human and drug trafficking, cybercrime and extortion, as well as on the extradition of criminal offenders.PM Modi and Carney had previously discussed bilateral relations during meetings in New Delhi in March and on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Évian in June.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi says he has spoken with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. The two leaders agreed to build on the positive momentum in India- Canada ties. Talks will focus on trade, energy, technology, security and people- to-people ties.

Article Title: Over half of Amaha clients live with mental health concerns for a year before seeking help; 56% report self-harm thoughts
Article Text:
Many people struggle with mental health issues for over a year before seeking professional help

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Mental health concerns can persist for months, sometimes years, before people seek professional help. By then, the distress may be affecting their relationships, work and ability to manage everyday tasks. More than half of people who eventually sought care had lived with their concerns for over a year, while 56.2% reported thoughts of self-harm before reaching professional support, according to the Amaha Mental Health Report 2026.The report is based on responses from 13,825 people who answered questions before beginning care with the mental healthcare provider between October 2025 and September 2026. Only 11.3% sought help within a month of experiencing mental health concerns.Dr Amit Malik, psychiatrist, founder and CEO of Amaha, said, “India’s progress in mental health must be judged by whether people can get timely, effective care, not simply by how openly we talk about it. These are the accounts of people who reached us; they should make us ask who is still unable to access care.”He added that friends, families and communities were vital to helping people recognise their needs and find care, and said finding treatment should not become “another test of a person’s resilience”.Nearly 95% of respondents reported at least two concerns, averaging five each. Anxiety was most common (72.1%), followed by stress (67.5%), low mood (58.3%), relationship difficulties (55.6%) and sleep disturbances in over a third. The report also found a gap between self-reported distress and clinical diagnosis: 33% of those initially reporting stress were later diagnosed with depression, while among those reporting repetitive thoughts and behaviours, 32% were diagnosed with depression and 11% with obsessive-compulsive disorder.Before approaching a professional, many respondents relied on informal support or tried to manage their concerns on their own. More than half (54.5%) had spoken to friends or family, while 44.6% had turned to self-help resources such as books, apps, videos and online communities. Nearly a third had tried therapy previously, and 19.4% had used prescribed medication.Avoidant coping strategies, including excessive screen time, oversleeping and overworking, were reported by 82.7%. Another 15.4% said they had turned to alcohol or other harmful substances instead of professional support.The impact extended to everyday functioning. Only 12.3% said they could manage all their daily tasks, while 27.3% said they could not manage most tasks or any at all.Young adults and working professionals formed the bulk of the cohort. Those aged 25–34 accounted for 51.3% of respondents, followed by 26.9% aged 18–24. Working professionals made up 64.3%, while students accounted for 15.3% and unemployed people 7.9%.Friends were the most frequently named contact in a mental health crisis (33.9%), followed by spouses (20.5%) and siblings (18.1%), underscoring the role of family and social networks in recognising distress and helping people access care.
Article Summary: Mental health concerns can persist for months, sometimes years, before people seek professional help. More than half of people who eventually sought care had lived with their concerns for over a year. Only 11.3% sought help within a month of experiencing mental health concerns.

Article Title: US secretary of state Rubio to travel to India next week; energy, strategic partnership and investment in focus

NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio will visit Mumbai and Jamnagar from October 17 to 22 as part of a trip to India and Uzbekistan, with talks in India set to focus on strengthening bilateral strategic ties and expanding energy cooperation.According to a media note issued by the US department of state, Rubio will travel to Samarkand in Uzbekistan before arriving in India for his second official visit to the country this year.During his India visit, Rubio is set to meet senior government officials to strengthen the US-India strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global developments, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation. He will also meet business leaders to explore opportunities for commercial investment and economic cooperation between the two countries.Before travelling to India, Rubio will participate in the C5+1 Ministerial in Uzbekistan, where he is expected to highlight strategic cooperation between Washington and the five Central Asian countries: Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and the Kyrgyz Republic.Rubio will also hold bilateral meetings with senior officials from the participating countries. The Uzbekistan leg of his trip will include a US commercial delegation comprising more than 200 business leaders, aimed at strengthening commercial ties between the United States and Central Asia.The visit comes as New Delhi and Washington resume high-level engagement. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said on Monday that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US president Donald Trump had spoken the previous week, adding that further developments in bilateral ties were expected.Speaking at an event in Kolkata marking the 250th anniversary of American independence, Gor highlighted cooperation between the two countries in defence, information technology and healthcare.He pointed to recent military exercises involving Indian and American forces, as well as the presence of US F-35 aircraft in Rajasthan for the first time. Gor also cited cross-border investments and India's role as a supplier of generic pharmaceuticals to the US.Rubio last visited India from May 23 to 26.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio will visit Mumbai and Jamnagar from October 17-22. Talks in India set to focus on strengthening bilateral strategic ties and expanding energy cooperation. Rubio will travel to Samarkand in Uzbekistan before arriving in India.

Article Title: Sensex jumps 1100 after finance minister's remarks spark LTCG cut hopes
Article Text:
RBI steps to check rupee volatility: FM

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman Tuesday said the govt was open and keen to "hear" discussions around the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax as it was "healthy" to have the debate.The minister, however, declined to be specific on the matter as preparations for the Union Budget in Feb are already underway.The FM's comments raised investors' hopes of a reduction in LTCG tax and securities transaction tax (STT), a longstanding demand among foreign funds who have been big sellers in the Indian market in the last two years.As a result, after a steady start, stock prices jumped with the sensex finally settling 1.5% or 1,109 points up at 73,034 points while Nifty closed 1.6% or 359 points up at 22,722 points.While responding to an observation that investors, especially foreign funds, were keen on removal of capital gains tax and streamlining of taxation before they started investing in India, Sitharaman said, "Two years ago, we had bought all the asset classes similarly and people thought that I was increasing the tax. I was not increasing the tax, I was bringing all of them at par, so that an investor is not speculating as to which one gives them greater leverage.So, these are the things on which there is a lot of debate. It's healthy to have this debate and I will be keen to hear them."At a Bloomberg event, FM acknowledged that investors, both within and outside, were commenting on LTCG and the question of treating all asset classes similarly has been a widely discussed topic.So far this year, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have bet sold Indian stocks worth a little over Rs 3 lakh crore, NSDL data showed. In 2025, the corresponding figure was a net outflow of nearly Rs 1.7 lakh crore and just Rs 427 crore in 2024. Since Sept 2024, sensex has lost about 13%.At the same event, Sitharaman also noted that rupee has depreciated "significantly" over the past year and a half, and RBI will continue its efforts to prevent excessive volatility. "RBI is not trying to fix the rupee, it is trying to stop the volatility, and for that there is a lot of effort from their side. I am sure RBI will take further steps to make sure that rupee does not become too volatile," she said in response to a query on capital outflows, especially in the equity market due to currency depreciation.FM stressed that govt has kept the economy on a sound footing and been careful with its spending and borrowings, helping investors looking to diversify away from China. "Fiscal discipline is not going to be a matter which should worry investors," she said, adding that domestic private capital is moving in and is attracting private capital from elsewhere as well.At a time when foreign funds are taking money out of India at a fast clip, a relook at the taxes related to the markets is a welcome move.According to Hitesh Sawhney, partner at Price Waterhouse, against the current backdrop of sustained foreign investor selling, elevated global yields and capital moving towards competing markets, revisiting LTCG taxation may be timely."A (zero) tax rate on LTCG, linked to a relatively longer holding period, could reward patient capital, encourage investors to remain invested in India and strengthen India's relative capital market attractiveness. It would also reduce foreign investors' dependence on treaty-based exemptions and the resulting uncertainty over treaty eligibility."
Article Summary: Nirmala Sitharaman says govt is open and keen to "hear" discussions around the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax. FM's comments raised investors' hopes of a reduction in LTCG tax and securities transaction tax (STT)

Article Title: INDIA bloc challenges SIR process but not its validity
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Why did opposition INDIA bloc, after making special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls the central point of its attack on Election Commission and govt, give up the challenge to the constitutional and statutory validity of SIR in their joint writ petition before Supreme Court Opposition members, led by LoP Rahul Gandhi, stated in the petition that they were not challenging SIR's validity in view of the SC judgement on Bihar SIR, which was conducted by EC based on its June 24, 2025, decision.That could be because SC in its May 27 judgement had examined the following questions - whether EC had the power to conduct SIR, whether SIR had a legitimate purpose and the process was proportionate to the object to be achieved, and whether the SIR procedure was contrary to Representation of the People Act and Registration of Electors Act, 1960 - and found there was nothing amiss in SIR's conduct or the process adopted to achieve the objective of weeding out voters who have died, shifted base or duplicate voters.SC had categorically ruled that SIR exercise "neither stands in direct conflict with RP Act and the 1960 Rules, nor does it detract from the constitutional imperative of free and fair elections".It had said, "The impugned SIR exercise, as conducted, satisfies requirements of proportionality. The measures adopted bear a rational nexus to the objective sought to be achieved, are not manifestly excessive, and are accompanied by sufficient procedural safeguards to prevent arbitrary exclusion."Since the judgement was of May 27, and attained finality as no one sought its review or correction, the INDIA bloc petitioners could not have challenged SIR's validity, thus limiting their challenge to alleged irregularities in the process of SIR and large-scale deletion of voters without giving them proper opportunity to rebut deletion.SC, in its five-month-old judgement, had said, "The statutory framework of RP Act itself provides for a situation where EC may direct a special revision under Section 21(3), in such manner as it may think fit and for reasons to be recorded."It also said "a reading of the impugned order, dated June 24, 2025, reveals EC has recorded the basis" on which it decided to conduct SIR. "We are equally satisfied that, in its object and design, the impugned SIR bears a direct nexus to the constitutional goal of a free and fair election. Free and fair elections do not rest merely upon the mechanics of polling. They equally depend upon the integrity, accuracy and purity of the electoral roll which forms the foundation of the democratic process," it had said."The impugned SIR, therefore, is not a process designed to subvert the established procedure, but one intended to secure the constitutional mandate of free and fair elections by ensuring the roll on which election rests is accurate and reliable," it had said, adding SIR had a direct nexus with the object of ensuring purity and accuracy of the electoral roll.
Article Summary: Opposition made special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls the central point of its attack on Election Commission and govt. Opposition members, led by LoP Rahul Gandhi, stated in the petition that they were not challenging SIR's validity in view of the SC judgement.

Article Title: Generate questions at last minute to prevent paper leaks: Nilekani
Article Text:
Nilekani: Need to expand comp-based testing infrastructure

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Question papers for high-stakes entrance examinations could be generated at the last minute from a massive bank of questions instead of being prepared and stored in advance, as part of a technology-driven overhaul to prevent leaks, Nandan Nilekani , chairperson of the high-powered task force on examination reforms, said on Tuesday. He also said PM Modi was keen to implement the panel's recommendations.Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026 in Delhi, the Infosys chairperson questioned the need for a fixed question paper, arguing that its existence created an economic incentive for theft and sale."Why do we need to have something called a question paper? Because the moment you have a question paper, that creates an economic incentive for that to be sold," Nilekani said. He suggested creating a massive question bank from which the paper would be assembled just before the examination. This, he said, would eliminate the incentive for advance leaks.Asked whether artificial intelligence could generate papers on examination day, Nandan Nilekani, replied, "Yeah, sure." The proposal comes as the six-member task force prepares to submit its report later this month, following extensive consultations on examination security, technology and governance.TOI reported on Oct 1 that the panel was prioritising "debundling" examination responsibilities by separating question-paper setting, exam conduct, test-centre management and security among different agencies. The restructuring seeks to reduce concentration of control over exams. A common calendar for major recruitment and entrance tests is also under consideration.Earlier, on Sept 16, TOI reported that multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance examinations and better-equipped, secure testing centres were among the prominent suggestions received by the task force. The recommendations included reliable electricity, internet connectivity, biometric verification and CCTV surveillance.He also stressed expanding computer-based testing infrastructure. He said the existing network of around 1.5 lakh testing locations needed to grow to accommodate a wider shift towards computer-based examinations."If you look at it systematically and go to root causes of why it's happening and use technology to solve it... they are solvable issues," he said.Constituted on July 26 following the NEET-UG controversy and the student protests, the task force has held around 18 panel meetings and 40 consultations. It has received over 50,000 suggestions from students, parents, professional associations and examination bodies.
Article Summary: Nandan Nilekani, chairperson of high-powered task force on examination reforms, said PM Modi was keen to implement the panel's recommendations. He suggested creating a massive question bank from which the paper would be assembled just before the examination. This, he said, would eliminate the incentive for advance leaks.

The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has found the missing head of an 11th-century Vishnu idol at Khajuraho, whose restoration became the subject of a recent controversy involving the Supreme Court, and plans to reattach it after expert examination. ASI has also introduced a three-year deadline for archaeological excavations to curb delays in research and cut approval times for most conservation projects to 15-20 days, director general Yadubir Singh Rawat told TOI in an exclusive interview. He also revealed plans for a preliminary excavation at Ujjain's Vaishya Tekri, where a Buddhist stupa could be larger than Sanchi's, although its actual scale and significance remain to be established.Controversy over the beheaded Vishnu idol at Khajuraho's Javari temple reached the Supreme Court last year when advocate Rakesh Dalal sought restoration, replacement or reconstruction of the seven-foot statue. While dismissing the petition, then CJI BR Gavai had said, "Go and ask the deity itself to do something now." Though Gavai later said he respects all religions and that his statement was taken out of context, a lawyer had tried to throw a shoe at him inside the courtroom.Rawat said the missing head had been found in an ASI store. "During a visit to Bhopal for the Brics summit, I learnt that the statue's head - which had been kept in our store - had been found. The person in charge informed me that someone likely tried to break off the head to steal it but failed to do so. We are having experts examine it and will soon reattach it to the statue."On encroachments at protected monuments, Rawat said "The root of this problem lies in the list prepared by British rulers in 1904 under the 'Ancient Monuments Preservation Act' - a list that the then govt adopted post-Independence without any review. The British had included cemeteries and graves of their obscure soldiers, horses and pets - which they deemed highly significant - among protected monuments." Rawat said a review in 1953 incorporated state monuments into a definitive list, but the central list remained unchanged. The resulting difficulties led to 17 monuments being removed from it.Regarding funding disparities, he said allocations depended on visitor numbers, maintenance requirements, security expenses and public facilities. Taj Mahal and Red Fort, he said, served as showcases for ASI, while Taj Mahal's maintenance required substantial expenditure because of its delicate structure and heavy tourist footfall. ASI paid around Rs 3 crore monthly for more than 200 CISF personnel deployed there.He said ASI circles had been instructed to prepare conservation and tourism development proposals for lesser-known sites like Bareilly's pyramid-like Bhim ki Gada structure.
Article Summary: Archaeological Survey of India has found the missing head of an 11th-century Vishnu idol at Khajuraho. The restoration became the subject of a recent controversy involving the Supreme Court. Director general Yadubir Singh Rawat revealed plans for a preliminary excavation at Ujjain's Vaishya Tekri.

Article Title: Centre asks states to go into ‘mission mode’ to curb stubble burning as farm fires rise in MP, Rajasthan
Article Text:
Centre steps up anti-stubble burning drive ahead of peak crop residue season (representative image)

Farm fires surge in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan

Farmers need affordable alternatives, says Centre

Centre flags idle crop residue machines

Monitoring to intensify after 3 pm

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Tuesday asked Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab Haryana and Delhi-NCR authorities to work in “mission mode” to prevent stubble burning ahead of the peak crop residue burning season, flagging a sharp rise in farm fires in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and environment minister Bhupender Yadav chaired a high-level inter-ministerial meeting with state agriculture ministers and officials to review crop residue management and measures to control farm fires.“Very little time remains between the harvesting of the current crop and the sowing of the rabi crop. Therefore, the administrative machinery must step away from paperwork and work directly on the ground on a war footing,” the two ministers said, according to a statement from the agriculture ministry.States have been directed to hold immediate meetings with district magistrates to ensure strict monitoring and implement practical solutions, the ministry said.Reviewing data from September 15 to October 12, Chouhan noted that stubble-burning incidents had declined by 53.3% in Haryana and around 32% in Uttar Pradesh compared with the corresponding period last year. Punjab had also recorded a fall.However, the rise in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan prompted concern.Madhya Pradesh's farm-fire count increased from 55 to 277, a jump of 452%, while Rajasthan's tally rose from 20 to 60, an increase of 200%.Chouhan directed the two states to identify affected districts and villages and immediately prepare special action plans. He also cautioned states reporting fewer incidents against becoming complacent, as a substantial portion of the harvest was still pending.The latest figures reflect the uneven spread of farm fires across northern and central India.Madhya Pradesh recorded 277 incidents by October 11, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 121 and Punjab with 118. Rajasthan reported 45 cases, Haryana seven, Uttarakhand three and Delhi one, taking the total across the seven states to 572.Stubble burning had been detected in 87 districts by October 11, with Amritsar recording 60 incidents, the highest among the seven states covered.Chouhan said farmers had only 20-25 days between paddy harvesting and wheat sowing, making burning a quick and inexpensive way to clear fields despite its impact on soil nutrients, soil organisms and air quality in Delhi-NCR.“Simply telling farmers not to burn stubble is insufficient; we must provide them with easy, accessible and affordable alternatives,” he said.He said crop residue could be incorporated into the soil to serve as organic manure or removed for use in bio-CNG, bio-ethanol, electricity generation and fodder production.The government also aims to develop a system in which farmers can benefit from environmentally friendly practices, including through carbon credits.Chouhan urged states to promote short-duration crop varieties, including Pusa 2090 and PR126, instead of longer-duration varieties such as Pusa-44, to give farmers sufficient time to clear fields before the next sowing season.The Centre has supplied more than 3.54 lakh crop residue management machines to states, including 26,109 during the current financial year. However, a central survey found that around 40% of older machines in Punjab and 48% in Haryana were idle or non-functional, news agency PTI reported.Chouhan directed states to repair existing machines alongside distributing new ones. He also called for the activation of Custom Hiring Centres to ensure that small and marginal farmers could access machinery at affordable rates.Between 2018-19 and 2025-26, the Centre released Rs 4,266.47 crore to states under the Crop Residue Management scheme. Punjab received Rs 2,056.50 crore, Haryana Rs 1,171.71 crore, Uttar Pradesh Rs 868.67 crore and Madhya Pradesh Rs 59 crore.For 2026-27, Rs 592.57 crore has been allocated, of which Rs 430.87 crore has been released.Chouhan expressed concern over slow utilisation of funds and urged Punjab to submit utilisation certificates for earlier releases so that the next instalment could be cleared without delay.Yadav called for stronger enforcement and ground-level monitoring, identifying key districts in Punjab and Haryana for closer scrutiny.In Punjab, these include Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Amritsar, Patiala and Gurdaspur. In Haryana, the focus districts are Kaithal, Karnal, Kurukshetra, Ambala and Fatehabad.He stressed the need to integrate stubble-burning data with the Commission for Air Quality Management and the Central Pollution Control Board, while tracking harvesting schedules and weather conditions that affect air quality in the National Capital Region.Yadav said monitoring should not rely on satellite data alone. District collectors should conduct ground assessments, while enforcement measures should include patrolling and flying squads, particularly after 3 pm, when satellites do not pass over the region.Chouhan also called for direct supply chains connecting farmers with thermal power plants that use stubble pellets for co-firing, compressed bio-gas plants and second-generation bio-ethanol facilities. He urged states to implement approved supply projects without delay and asked drought-hit regions to store crop residue safely for use as livestock fodder.The ministers said state governments would remain responsible for implementation, with the Centre providing technical, administrative and financial support.
Article Summary: Centre steps up anti-stubble burning drive ahead of peak crop residue season. Farm fires surge in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab Haryana and Delhi-NCR. Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and environment minister Bhupender Yadav chaired high-level meeting.

Article Title: 'Absence from draft SIR doesn't mean deletion': EC to Bombay HC
Article Text:
The Election Commission of India clarified that missing names from the draft electoral roll during the Special Intensive Revision do not imply their deletion.

ECI clarifies the nature of the SIR exercise

Petitioner’s lawyer recounts timeline of events

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Form 8 rejected after deadline for objections

The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Tuesday told the Bombay high court that a voter's name missing from the draft electoral roll prepared during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) does not automatically imply deletion. The court reserved its judgment on a writ petition filed by a Goa resident.Senior Advocate Ashutosh Kumbhakoni, appearing for the ECI, told the Goa bench that the SIR involves preparing the electoral roll afresh, unlike a Special Summary Revision (SSR), which focuses on updating an existing list.The bench, comprising Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar, reserved its verdict after hearing arguments in the matter. The hearing took place amid an ongoing controversy over the SIR exercise and the functioning of the ECI.Paresh Salgaonkar and five members of his family, who live in the St Cruz constituency of North Goa district, had approached the court alleging that their names were removed from the electoral roll during the revision process.Kumbhakoni submitted that an SIR is a comprehensive, de novo exercise in which the electoral roll is prepared from scratch.In contrast, a summary revision updates the existing electoral roll on the basis of information received through the prescribed procedure.“Absence from the draft SIR roll does not automatically amount to deletion,” the ECI lawyer said, maintaining that a name missing from a draft list being prepared afresh could not technically be described as deleted.The lawyer further argued that the petitioner had allegedly not lived at the address recorded in the electoral rolls before the SIR for eight to 10 years. He also contended that the petitioner had not applied for an address change before the revision exercise began.“In fact, my lord, this is a classical case which shows the effectiveness of SIR,” Kumbhakoni told the court.According to the news agency PTI, the judges observed that they had made it clear from the outset that the petition did not challenge the SIR process itself.Advocate Vivek Rodrigues, representing the petitioner, detailed the events surrounding the enumeration exercise and the subsequent absence of the petitioner's name from the draft electoral roll.Rodrigues said the enumeration process began on November 4, 2025. The Booth Level Officer (BLO) visited both the petitioner's former and current addresses on November 8.On November 12, the petitioner contacted the BLO to request an enumeration form. However, the officer declined, saying the form had to be delivered to the address listed in the electoral roll, which was the petitioner's previous residence.The petitioner later submitted Form 8 to seek a change of address. The ECI acknowledged receipt of the application on December 8, 2025. However, the petitioner's name was absent when the draft electoral roll was published on December 16, Rodrigues told the court.The BLO subsequently informed the petitioner that the Form 8 application was still being processed and had not been rejected.Rodrigues said the petitioner received a letter from the ECI on January 17, 2026, informing him that his address-change application had been forwarded to the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO).The final date for submitting objections to the draft electoral roll was January 19. However, the petitioner's application was rejected on January 21, after the deadline had passed.“On January 21, my application is rejected. So I am neither in the boat nor in the canoe, left in the sea,” Rodrigues argued before the bench.
Article Summary: ECI tells Bombay high court that a voter's name missing from the draft electoral roll does not automatically imply deletion. The court reserved its judgment on a writ petition filed by a Goa resident. The hearing took place amid an ongoing controversy over the SIR exercise and the functioning of the ECI.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.
